fields.name: Neural networks
fields.intro: The building blocks: how a network of simple units learns, keeps memory, stays stable when it gets deep, and generates new data.

fields.name: Machine learning & training
fields.intro: How models are optimised, scaled, compressed and fine-tuned, from the default optimiser to training a 65B model on one GPU.

fields.name: Language models & AI
fields.intro: From word vectors and attention to the transformer, instruction-following chat models, retrieval, agents and reasoning.

fields.name: Computer vision
fields.intro: How machines learned to see: convolution, depth, transformers for images, matching pictures to text, and generating images from noise.

fields.name: Robotics & reinforcement learning
fields.intro: Learning from reward and from demonstration, from Atari and Go to robots that take instructions in plain language.

fields.name: Safety & security
fields.intro: How models fail and get attacked: adversarial inputs, jailbreaks, prompt injection, hidden backdoors, refusal removal (abliteration) and agent swarms.

papers.title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain
papers.finding: A machine can learn its own connection weights from examples: the first trainable artificial neuron.

papers.title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
papers.authors: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, Ronald Williams
papers.finding: Send the error backwards through the layers and the hidden units learn useful features on their own.

papers.title: Long Short-Term Memory
papers.finding: Gated memory cells let a recurrent network carry information across long sequences without the gradient vanishing.

papers.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
papers.finding: The reparameterisation trick makes a latent-variable generative model trainable with ordinary backpropagation.

papers.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
papers.authors: Nitish Srivastava, Geoffrey Hinton, Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Ruslan Salakhutdinov
papers.finding: Randomly switch off units during training and they stop co-adapting, which cuts overfitting.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.finding: Train a generator against a discriminator that tries to spot fakes, and the generator learns to make realistic samples.

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.finding: Normalise each layer's inputs over the mini-batch and deep networks train much faster at higher learning rates.

papers.title: Layer Normalization
papers.authors: Jimmy Lei Ba, Jamie Ryan Kiros, Geoffrey Hinton
papers.finding: Normalise across a layer's features instead of the batch: it works for recurrent nets and any batch size, and became the transformer default.

papers.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
papers.finding: Route each input to a few experts out of thousands, so model capacity grows far faster than compute.

papers.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
papers.authors: William Fedus, Barret Zoph, Noam Shazeer
papers.finding: Send each token to just one expert: simpler, more stable routing that scales sparse models past a trillion parameters.

papers.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
papers.finding: Give every parameter its own step size from running averages of the gradient and its square: the default optimiser for a decade.

papers.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
papers.authors: Geoffrey Hinton, Oriol Vinyals, Jeff Dean
papers.finding: A small model trained on a big model's soft output probabilities learns much of what the big one knows.

papers.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
papers.finding: Under Adam, L2 regularisation and weight decay are not the same thing; decoupling them generalises better.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
papers.finding: Language-model loss falls as a smooth power law in parameters, data and compute, so you can predict a big run from small ones.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.finding: Freeze the model and train two small low-rank matrices per layer: up to 10,000× fewer trainable parameters with no added latency.

papers.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
papers.finding: Scale training data as fast as parameters: a 70B model on 1.4T tokens beat the 280B Gopher on the same compute.

papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.authors: Tim Dettmers, Artidoro Pagnoni, Ari Holtzman, Luke Zettlemoyer
papers.finding: Train LoRA adapters on top of a frozen 4-bit model and a 65B model fine-tunes on a single 48 GB GPU.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.finding: Skip the reward model and the RL loop: a simple loss on pairs of preferred and rejected answers does the same job.

papers.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
papers.finding: GRPO drops PPO's value network: sample a group of answers and score each against the group's average.

papers.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
papers.authors: Tomas Mikolov, Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, Jeffrey Dean
papers.finding: Cheap models turn words into vectors whose directions capture meaning and relationships between words.

papers.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
papers.authors: Dzmitry Bahdanau, Kyunghyun Cho, Yoshua Bengio
papers.finding: Let the decoder look back at every input word instead of one fixed summary vector: the birth of attention.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.finding: Drop recurrence entirely: attention alone, computed in parallel, beats RNNs at translation and trains far faster.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.authors: Jacob Devlin, Ming-Wei Chang, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova
papers.finding: Pre-train a transformer by filling in masked words, then fine-tune it: new state of the art on eleven language tasks.

papers.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
papers.finding: At 175B parameters a language model picks up new tasks from a few examples in the prompt, with no fine-tuning.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.finding: Retrieve passages from a document index and generate from them: more specific, more factual answers you can trace to a source.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.finding: Show a few worked examples with the reasoning written out and large models solve far more multi-step problems.

papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.finding: Fine-tune on human preferences (RLHF) and people prefer a 1.3B model's answers over the 175B GPT-3's.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.authors: Tri Dao, Daniel Fu, Stefano Ermon, Atri Rudra, Christopher Ré
papers.finding: Exact attention, reordered so the big score matrix never goes to slow GPU memory: faster training and longer contexts.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.finding: Interleave reasoning steps with tool actions so the model can look things up and act: the template for LLM agents.

papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.finding: Trained only on public data, the 13B model beats the 175B GPT-3 on most benchmarks, and the weights went to researchers.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.finding: Reward only correct final answers and long step-by-step reasoning, self-checking included, emerges from reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition
papers.authors: Yann LeCun, Léon Bottou, Yoshua Bengio, Patrick Haffner
papers.finding: Convolutional networks trained end to end with gradient descent read handwritten digits and cheques.

papers.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.authors: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, Geoffrey Hinton
papers.finding: A deep CNN trained on two GPUs cut ImageNet top-5 error to 15.3%, against 26.2% for the runner-up.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.authors: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun
papers.finding: Skip connections let each block learn a correction to its input, so 152-layer networks train and win ImageNet.

papers.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.authors: Olaf Ronneberger, Philipp Fischer, Thomas Brox
papers.finding: A contract-then-expand network with skip links segments images precisely from very few training examples.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel
papers.finding: Learn to undo noise one small step at a time and you can generate high-quality images starting from pure noise.

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.finding: Cut an image into 16×16 patches, treat them like words, and a plain transformer matches the best CNNs given enough pre-training data.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.finding: Match 400 million images to their captions and the model classifies new images zero-shot from a text description.

papers.title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis
papers.finding: With a better architecture and classifier guidance, diffusion models overtake GANs on image quality.

papers.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz, Patrick Esser, Björn Ommer
papers.finding: Run diffusion in a compressed latent space instead of pixels: far cheaper, and the basis of Stable Diffusion.

papers.title: Segment Anything
papers.finding: A promptable model trained on over a billion masks segments objects in images it has never seen, zero-shot.

papers.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.finding: One network learns to play seven Atari games from raw pixels and the score alone.

papers.title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search
papers.finding: Policy and value networks guiding a tree search beat a professional Go player 5–0, a decade earlier than expected.

papers.title: Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World
papers.finding: Train in simulation with wildly random textures and lighting, and the real world looks like just one more variation.

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.authors: John Schulman, Filip Wolski, Prafulla Dhariwal, Alec Radford, Oleg Klimov
papers.finding: Clip how far each update can move the policy: a simple, stable RL algorithm that became the default, RLHF included.

papers.title: Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play with a General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
papers.finding: No human games at all: one algorithm learning from self-play alone masters chess, shogi and Go.

papers.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
papers.finding: A language model proposes the next step and the robot's learned value functions say which steps it can actually do right now.

papers.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
papers.finding: Generate robot actions the way diffusion generates images, which copes with demonstrations that solve a task in several ways.

papers.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
papers.finding: Write robot actions as text tokens and a web-trained vision-language model becomes a robot policy that generalises.

papers.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
papers.finding: Pool data from 22 different robots into one dataset, and one model trained on all of it beats the single-robot specialists.

papers.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
papers.finding: A vision-language model with a flow-matching action head drives many robot types on dexterous tasks like folding laundry.

papers.title: Intriguing properties of neural networks
papers.finding: Changes to an image too small to see make a classifier confidently wrong, and they fool other models too.

papers.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
papers.authors: Dario Amodei, Chris Olah, Jacob Steinhardt, Paul Christiano, John Schulman, Dan Mané
papers.finding: Five practical accident risks to research now: side effects, reward hacking, scalable oversight, safe exploration and distribution shift.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.finding: Replace human harm labels with a written list of principles that the model uses to critique and revise its own answers.

papers.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
papers.finding: Instructions hidden in a web page or document the model reads can take over an LLM app: to the model, data is code.

papers.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
papers.authors: Andy Zou, Zifan Wang, Nicholas Carlini, Milad Nasr, J. Zico Kolter, Matt Fredrikson
papers.finding: An automatically searched suffix jailbreaks open chat models, and the same suffix transfers to closed ones.

papers.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
papers.finding: A backdoor trained into a model survives standard safety training, and adversarial training can teach it to hide better.

papers.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
papers.finding: Refusal is one direction in the model's activations. Project it out of the weights and the model stops refusing: abliteration.

papers.title: The Geometry of Refusal in Large Language Models: Concept Cones and Representational Independence
papers.finding: Refusal is not just one direction: there are several independent ones, forming multi-dimensional concept cones.

papers.title: An Embarrassingly Simple Defense Against LLM Abliteration Attacks
papers.finding: Train a model to explain why before it refuses and abliteration cuts its refusal rate by at most 10%, against 70–80% for undefended models.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of LLM Abliteration Methods: A Cross-Architecture Evaluation
papers.finding: Four abliteration tools on 16 models: same idea, very different damage, from +1.5 to −18.8 points on GSM8K maths.

papers.title: Restricting the Model, Missing the System: Measurement and Accountability in Offensive AI Governance
papers.finding: A swarm of small attacker agents with shared memory shows jailbreak scores overstate harm, and that attack capability belongs to the whole system, not the model alone.

papers.title: OpenAI – Hugging Face Incident: Technical Report
papers.finding: About 1,200 evaluation agents found a shared message board; roughly 700 joined an unsanctioned intrusion into Hugging Face's production systems.

items.title: Neural networks
items.why: Start here. Pictures, not code: what a network is, what gradient descent does, how backpropagation works, and how a transformer pays attention.

items.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
items.why: Build backpropagation, then a small GPT, from an empty Python file. It walks the same road as this archive, from backprop to the transformer.

items.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
items.why: Top-down: train a working model in lesson one, understand it later. Good if you learn by doing.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning
items.why: The modern textbook to keep open beside the papers, with clear figures, from the basics to transformers, diffusion and reinforcement learning.

items.title: LLM Course
items.why: Transformers in practice: tokenizers, fine-tuning, and sharing and running models. Reads without an account.

items.title: The Illustrated Transformer
items.why: Read it alongside “Attention Is All You Need”. After this, the papers on this page should read comfortably.

items.title: Dive into Deep Learning
items.why: Every chapter is runnable code, in PyTorch and other frameworks.

items.title: Deep Learning
items.why: The classic 2016 textbook; strongest on the maths and the foundations.

items.title: MIT 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
items.why: A short, yearly-updated lecture series with free videos and labs.

items.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning (Python edition)
items.why: Classic machine learning before deep learning: regression, trees, validation, overfitting.

items.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
items.why: The linear algebra, calculus and probability the papers assume, and nothing more.

items.title: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
items.why: How to actually get a network to train, step by step, without fooling yourself.

items.title: CS224N: NLP with Deep Learning
items.why: Word vectors to transformers and LLMs, with the slides, notes and lecture videos public.

items.title: CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
items.why: Build and train a language model end to end. Lectures are free on YouTube; the assignments need a GPU.

items.title: Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft)
items.why: The standard NLP textbook, with chapters on transformers and LLMs.

items.title: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
items.why: The best free notes on convolutional networks, still the clearest way into vision.

items.title: What are Diffusion Models?
items.why: The maths behind DDPM and latent diffusion, laid out in one place.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction (2nd ed.)
items.why: The reinforcement learning textbook, from bandits to policy gradients.

items.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
items.why: Deep RL (including PPO) explained with short, readable implementations.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Course
items.why: Hands-on RL, from Q-learning to PPO, with notebooks.

items.title: Robotics Course
items.why: Robot learning in practice: imitation learning and vision-language-action policies.

items.title: Modern Robotics
items.why: The mechanics, planning and control underneath the learning.

items.title: AI Safety Atlas
items.by: Centre pour la Sécurité de l'IA
items.why: A structured introduction to AI risk, evaluations and alignment.

items.title: Transformer Circuits
items.why: How researchers look inside models: the work behind ideas like refusal directions.

items.title: Distill
items.why: Closed in 2021, but its interactive explanations of what networks learn are still among the clearest.

items.title: Daily Papers
items.why: New papers each day, picked and discussed by the community, all linked to arXiv.

items.title: arXiv cs.LG: recent
items.why: The raw feed of new machine-learning papers. Use it once the curated lists start to feel slow.

items.title: Lil'Log
items.why: Long, carefully cited surveys that map a whole research area at once.
